agent_vs_you: The agent's plan matches mine in shape: an instrumental music bed and one assemble of the five photos in the attached order, 9:16, 10 s, no text. It asked assemble for 'smooth cross-dissolves' and 'fit photos without cropping' in extra, but the catalogue line for assemble mentions no transitions and the code ignores both: it concatenates with hard cuts and crops every photo to fill. The agent had no way to know its extra was dropped, and the tool reported success. The fail was then pinned on 'speech' in the soundtrack, which the evidence says is a transcription hallucination on instrumental music, not vocals. So the reel's real defect (hard cuts where the user asked for smooth transitions) is the harness's, and the grader failed it for the wrong reason.

your_plan.say: I'll cut your five café photos into a 10-second vertical reel in the order you attached them, 2 seconds each with a gentle push-in and soft dissolves between them, over a relaxed instrumental track. No text.

params.prompt_or_change: Relaxed instrumental cafe lounge music: soft acoustic guitar, mellow Rhodes piano, light brushed drums, warm and unhurried, about 85 BPM, gentle ending. Purely instrumental: no vocals, no singing, no humming, no spoken words.

steps.why: The bed; generated at the 15 s minimum and cut to the reel by code.

params.prompt_or_change: The five photos in the attached order, equal time each, a slow push-in on each, soft 0.5 s cross-dissolves between photos, music at full level fading out over the last second, no text.

steps.why: Code, 0 credits: exact order, length and aspect; the dissolves need the assemble fix below (today it hard-cuts).

fix: 1) Harness (assemble.js): support transitions: join the parts with xfade (fade/dissolve, 0.4-0.6 s) and lengthen each part by the overlap so the total stays exact; default to dissolves for a photo-only reel and to cuts only when asked; list 'transitions: cut | dissolve' on assemble's catalogue line. 2) Harness: when a step's extra asks for something the tool does not do (dissolves, fit without cropping), report it instead of returning success silently. 3) Grader: do not treat a few transcribed words over a music bed as singing; run a vocal/speech detector or re-transcribe with a 'this may be instrumental music' prompt and require a confident, sustained transcript before calling it speech; also sample frames around the cuts so transitions can be judged.
evidence: cafe-reel.mp4 is 720x1280, 10.0 s, with AAC audio. Frame-difference analysis gives four single-frame jumps (mean abs diff 70-95) at 2.03, 4.03, 6.03 and 8.03 s and no ramps: hard cuts, no dissolves. Frames at 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 s show storefront, latte, pastries, barista and interior in the attached order, each centre-cropped to fill 9:16 with a slow push-in (the barista's face half cut); all recognisable, no text. cafe-music.mp3 (10 s, peak -1.8 dB): its 0-4 kHz spectrogram shows only flat, steady instrument harmonics and a regular backbeat, with no gliding or vibrato harmonics and no syllable-rate formant bursts that singing or speech would leave. The transcriber returned '끄덕끄덕' here and 'Dieu, tu es grand' for a different music file in run real-1: random-language fragments, the usual hallucination on instrumental audio.
